sensitivity_excluding_bd_ready.note: sessions consisting only of bd ready become empty here and drop out rather than counting as zero

G3_enumeration_cost.method: For each C1 (label-containment) query the BDP-expressible superset is that query with the label predicate removed. Historical result sizes cannot be recovered, so superset SHAPES are counted exactly and their sizes are measured against one present-day store as a proxy.

present_day_store_proxy.caveat: One store at one time, and it is the analyst's own project. The corpus spans 118 distinct working directories whose collection sizes are not measured here. This supports a claim about collections of this scale (low thousands of resources), not a general property of limit and cursor.

deviations_from_preregistration.registered: resolve session ids via gc session logs from the rig root
deviations_from_preregistration.actual: enumerated transcript JSONL directly from the on-disk agent project directories (9,172 files, 6.8 GB)
deviations_from_preregistration.direction: larger denominator than the registered procedure would yield

deviations_from_preregistration.registered: a batched model pass over free-text search arguments
deviations_from_preregistration.actual: not run. The mechanical rule assigns N1 to every positional argument on `bd search` that is not a generated bd id. A model pass could only move arguments OUT of N1, so G1 as computed is an upper bound on the text-search residue rather than an estimate of it, and it still lands below the profile-adequate threshold.
deviations_from_preregistration.direction: conservative against the study's own null result

deviations_from_preregistration.registered: median and p90 superset size a C1 query must enumerate
deviations_from_preregistration.actual: superset SHAPES counted exactly, with their sizes measured against one present-day store as a proxy. Historical result sizes are not recoverable from transcripts: the size a query returned on the day it ran is not recorded anywhere, and stores have changed since.
deviations_from_preregistration.direction: descriptive either way; G3 carries no threshold, but the substituted statistic answers 'what must be enumerated' by shape rather than by measured size

deviations_from_preregistration.actual: queries carrying no predicate at all are reported as E_NONE rather than folded into E1. They remain expressible (the empty selector matches the whole collection) and no gate keys on this split.
deviations_from_preregistration.direction: reporting granularity only; no gate affected

classifier_defects_found_and_fixed: bd dep add/remove counted as reads (dep is a read subcommand only for list/tree/show/graph/why/path/cycles)
the id pattern rejected multi-hyphen ids such as agent-diagnostics-4w02, sending 1,489 identity fetches to 'unparseable'
--help invocations were classified as retrieval queries (612 of them)
shell redirection tokens (2>&1) were read as argv placeholders, which at one point discarded 27,939 of 31,133 rows
--search, --unassigned and --mol were absent from the flag table

defects_found_by_independent_review.note: Two independent reviewers audited the classifier and the method after the first result was committed. Every defect below is fixed in the scripts published here, and the numbers in this file are post-fix.

changed_a_published_number.defect: the id pattern matched any hyphenated lowercase token, so a free-text topic query on `bd search` scored as an identity fetch (E0) instead of text (N1)
changed_a_published_number.effect: 88 positionals across 799 deduped `bd search` invocations moved from E0 to N1. G1 0.0105 -> 0.0114 session-averaged, 0.0464 -> 0.0508 per-invocation. Verdict unchanged.
changed_a_published_number.why_it_mattered: it undercounted the text residue, which is the one direction the writeup claimed was impossible

changed_a_published_number.defect: g3.py counted raw rows while every other statistic deduped exact repeats within a session
changed_a_published_number.effect: C1 invocations 577 -> 342, matching label_counts_deduped; retains-a-narrowing-predicate 91.9% -> 89.8%; bare 47 -> 35. Shape count and conclusion unchanged.
changed_a_published_number.why_it_mattered: analysis.json reported 342 and 577 for the same quantity

changed_a_published_number.defect: E3 fired whenever two labels co-occurred, including combinations containing an inexpressible one such as E1+N1
changed_a_published_number.why_it_mattered: the taxonomy defines E3 as a boolean combination of EXPRESSIBLE predicates; the loose rule inflated the expressible side with queries the Selector cannot serve

zero_measured_impact_on_this_corpus: `bd search --query TEXT` captured its value but never got an N1 label; no invocation in the corpus used that form (all 810 use the positional)
-s means --status on list/search but --sort on `bd ready`, which the flat flag table could not express; no corpus row hit the collision
ten subcommand-local boolean flags were absent from the valueless set, so each could have swallowed the token after it as a fake value
clustered short flags (-qv) parse as one unknown flag; the corpus contains no clustered short flag on a read subcommand
--spec-id was mapped but does not exist in the CLI (dead entry, removed)
known_and_unfixed: extract.py can build a fake argv from prose that merely contains the token bd. About 12 of 31,133 rows show this shape; 2 survived into the counted population, both as ordinary list --status shapes whose label is unaffected. No filter was added, because a prose detector here would be a semantic heuristic in a layer that is mechanical by design.
